review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped the formal-frontier sources for uses of the lemmas below. I found no rewrite cycles and no unsuitable simp orientations among the existing simp lemmas. The findings are about missing simp coverage in the point-class and functoriality lemmas. I did not run Lean. Whether the proposed attributes help in practice is untested, and I checked termination and confluence only by reading the statements.

findings.excerpt:
theorem singularHomologyZeroPoint_naturality {X Y : TopCat.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (x : X) :
    singularHomologyZeroPoint X x ≫ (integralSingularHomologyFunctor 0).map f =
      singularHomologyZeroPoint Y (f x)
findings.problem: This is the canonical normalisation for a point class pushed forward along a map. The right side is strictly simpler: the composite disappears and the point becomes `f x`. The sibling `singularHomologyZeroPoint_augmentation` is `simp`, but this lemma and its `_assoc` form are not. Every use is a manual `rw`: `rw [singularHomologyZeroPoint_naturality_assoc]` at line 198, and the doubled `rw [singularHomologyZeroPoint_naturality, singularHomologyZeroPoint_naturality]` at lines 786–787 in `twoPointReducedBasis_swap`, which needs a `simp [twoPointSwap]` afterwards. The proofs therefore interleave `simp only` and `rw` with exact term shapes, and other users of point classes must do the same.
findings.proposed_change: Mark it `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`. The rule terminates because the right side has no `≫`. It has no side conditions and is not in conflict with `singularHomologyZeroPoint_augmentation`. Then replace the two `rw` calls at 786–787 and the `rw ..._assoc` at 198 with `simp`. `twoPointSwap_apply` already rewrites `twoPointSwap b` to `!b`.
findings.benefit: Point-class computations normalise to `singularHomologyZeroPoint Y (f x)` automatically. The `twoPointReducedBasis_swap` proof gets shorter and no longer depends on rewrite counts. Later files that push point classes along maps (for example spheres) can use plain `simp`.

findings.excerpt:
@[reassoc]
theorem reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap_comp {X Y Z : TopCat.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap (f ≫ g) =
      reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap f ≫ reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap g
findings.problem: The sibling `reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap_id` is `@[simp]`, but the composition lemma is not. The simp interface for this map is therefore half-covered. `reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap (f ≫ g)` stays unexpanded, while the functor's `@[simps]` lemma `reducedSingularHomologyZeroFunctor_map` rewrites functor maps to this raw map. A goal built from the functor and `map_comp` therefore ends up in a form that `simp` cannot split. The proofs at lines 232 and 238–240 use `cancel_mono` plus `simp` on the `_ι` lemma, where one `simp` call with the `comp` lemma would do. Mathlib normally makes `map_comp`-style lemmas for such maps simp when the right side only splits a composite.
findings.proposed_change: Use `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]` on `reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap_comp`. The right side only decomposes the argument, so it terminates. It is consistent with `reducedSingularHomologyZeroMap_id` and with the `_ι` rule, which pushes the maps through `kernel.ι`.
findings.benefit: Composites of continuous maps are split into composites of reduced maps by `simp`. This matches the existing `_id` and `_ι` simp lemmas, so the two-point statements with `𝟙 twoPointSpace` or compositions of swaps can be handled without manual rewriting.

findings.excerpt:
theorem singularHomologyZeroPoint_twoPoint_iso (b : Bool) :
    singularHomologyZeroPoint twoPointSpace b ≫
        twoPointSingularHomologyZeroIso.hom =
      Sigma.ι (fun _ : Bool ↦ singularHomologyIntegerCoefficients) b
findings.problem: The two-point `H₀` iso gives a pair of `reassoc` rewrite rules, `point ≫ iso.hom = ι b` and `ι b ≫ iso.inv = point`. Neither is `simp`. Several later proofs have to name `singularHomologyZeroPoint_twoPoint_iso_assoc` explicitly. It appears twice in a `rw` at lines 670–671 and again in the simp sets at 743 and 747. `twoPoint_sigmaι_iso_inv` is used only through `simp` after a manual `rw ←` at line 612. The two rules are exact inverses on the same objects. Each rewrite turns a composite with the iso into a bare `Sigma.ι` or point class, so both are shrinking and the pair does not loop. Whether adding both as simp lemmas would conflict with the iso's own `hom_inv_id` simp lemmas is untested.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `singularHomologyZeroPoint_twoPoint_iso` and `twoPoint_sigmaι_iso_inv` with `@[reassoc (attr := simp)]`. Alternatively, keep them local and bundle them in a named `simp` set. Then drop the explicit `_assoc` entries from the simp calls in `twoPointReducedBasis_coordinate` and `twoPointReducedCoordinate_basis`.
findings.benefit: The two-point basis computations would no longer depend on which simp-set entries are listed. Each side of the iso would also have a documented normal form.
